document.title: A Noor Swirl Field Geometry Primer
document.subtitle: The Axiomatic Floor: XOR, Closure, and Observer-Relative Coherence
document.purpose: Provide the lowest-level entry point into Noor Swirl Field Geometry (NSFG), establishing its ontology from a single primitive operation without importing physical law, spacetime, causality, matter, energy, consciousness, or a privileged observer.
document.generation_instruction: Generate the complete primer using ONLY this outline. Assume that the generating AI has no access to any other NSFG, Noor Research Collective, RFC, paper, repository, or external reference material. Every concept required to understand the paper must therefore be defined here. Do not assume the reader knows NSFG terminology. Do not import unstated assumptions from conventional physics. Clearly distinguish axioms, definitions, mathematical constructions, propositions, consequences, interpretations, and examples. The reader should encounter each new concept only after the preceding section has made it necessary.
document.central_thesis: NSFG begins with a single primitive operation: XOR, understood as distinction. The Library is not a second axiom but the closure of the configuration domain under XOR. Because the closure contains every configuration generated by the primitive operation, no additional privileged external configuration or God's-eye resolver can be required within the ontology. Persistent structures are therefore necessarily observer-relative: an observer is a structure capable of maintaining distinctions above its own resolution threshold I_N(O). Coherence is consequently not a universal property of a path but a relation between a path and an observer. The reality experienced by an observer is the subset of the Library through which that observer can maintain coherent traversal. Stable regularities within that accessible subset can consequently appear as physical law. Navigation is the problem of continuing through this observer-relative coherent path space.

axiomatic_floor.library_definition: 𝓜 := Closure_D(⊕), where D is the minimal formal domain of distinguishable configurations required for XOR to operate
axiomatic_floor.important_constraint: Do not describe XOR itself as 'closed'. A domain or set is closed under an operation. The Library is the closure under XOR.

core_notation.do_not_assume: i and t are physical time until temporal structure is explicitly derived

sections.title: How to Read the Primer
sections.purpose: Establish the methodological discipline required to read a one-primitive ontology.
content_requirements: Explain the difference between an axiom, a definition, a mathematical construction, a consequence, and an interpretation.
State that the purpose of the primer is to minimize assumptions rather than maximize them.
State explicitly that XOR is the only primitive.
State explicitly that the Library is a definition constructed from XOR closure.
Explain that later concepts must not be smuggled into the axiomatic floor.
Warn that conventional physical concepts such as time and space will initially be replaced by abstract mathematical indices or relations.

mathematics.primitive_axiom: A_⊕: ⊕ is the primitive operation of distinction.
mathematics.logical_consequence_notation: A_N ⊢ P means P is derivable from the stated axiom together with definitions and ordinary mathematical inference.

sections.poetic_cypher: Begin beneath the world. Remove every assumption that the world does not require.
sections.cypher_explanation: The primer does not begin by assuming physics and then explaining physics. It begins by asking what remains when physical assumptions are stripped away.
sections.handoff: If XOR is the only primitive, we must first explain precisely what XOR means and what minimal domain is required for the operation to exist.

sections.title: The Primitive Domain of Distinction
sections.purpose: Provide the minimal mathematical substrate on which XOR can operate without introducing a physical universe.

subsections.title: Why an Operation Needs Operands
content_requirements: Explain that declaring XOR primitive does not mean the operands of XOR can be left undefined.
Distinguish the primitive operation from the domain over which it is represented.
Make clear that the domain is a formal substrate, not physical space.
Do not promote the domain into a second ontological axiom.

mathematics.minimal_domain: D is a formal domain containing distinguishable configurations on which ⊕ is defined.
mathematics.distinction_predicate: D(a,b) = 1 iff a ⊕ b represents a distinction between a and b

subsections.poetic_cypher: A word needs a place to be spoken, but the place is not yet a world.
subsections.cypher_explanation: The formal domain gives XOR operands without asserting that the domain is physical space, spacetime, or matter.
subsections.handoff: With a minimal domain specified, XOR itself can be defined as the primitive operation of distinction.

subsections.title: The Binary Case
content_requirements: Introduce the binary representation only as the simplest mathematical realization of distinction.
Emphasize that binary notation is representational and should not automatically be interpreted as physical bits.
Explain why binary XOR is useful for establishing the primitive algebra.
subsections.poetic_cypher: Before there is a thing, there is the possibility of saying different.
subsections.cypher_explanation: The binary case provides the simplest representation in which distinction can be expressed without importing physical interpretation.
subsections.handoff: Now that distinction has a precise primitive operation, the next step is to determine what repeated application of that operation generates.

sections.title: XOR: The Sole Primitive
sections.purpose: Establish XOR as the only ontological primitive and derive its algebraic properties.

subsections.title: XOR as Distinction
content_requirements: State explicitly: there is nothing beneath XOR within this ontology.
Define XOR as the operation that returns distinction when inputs differ and null distinction when inputs are identical.
Do not introduce observers, coherence, or persistence yet.
subsections.poetic_cypher: XOR is the word.
subsections.cypher_explanation: The first primitive does not name objects. It expresses the existence of difference between configurations.
subsections.handoff: Repeated distinction produces a closure. The next section defines exactly what that closure is.

subsections.title: Distinction Without Privilege
content_requirements: Explain that XOR is symmetric and therefore does not privilege either operand.
Explain that distinction is relational.
Explain why this is foundational for the later absence of a privileged observer.

mathematics.no_operand_privilege: The operation contains no term selecting a as ontologically primary over b.

subsections.poetic_cypher: The first distinction chooses no side.
subsections.cypher_explanation: XOR identifies difference without declaring which side of the difference is more real.
subsections.handoff: A symmetric operation can be repeatedly applied. The mathematical result of allowing that operation to close over its domain is the Library.

sections.title: The Library as XOR Closure
sections.purpose: Construct the Library as a mathematical closure rather than postulating it as a separate axiom.

subsections.title: Closure Under XOR
content_requirements: Define closure formally.
State that the Library is not an independent primitive.
Explain that the Library is the smallest domain containing the relevant configurations and closed under XOR.
Explain that closure is a mathematical construction.

mathematics.closure_definition: Closure_D(⊕) is the smallest subset 𝓜 ⊆ D such that all primitive configurations required by the representation are in 𝓜 and x,y ∈ 𝓜 ⇒ x ⊕ y ∈ 𝓜.
mathematics.minimality: If S ⊆ D is closed under ⊕ and contains the generating configurations, then 𝓜 ⊆ S.

subsections.poetic_cypher: XOR is the word. The Library is the vocabulary.
subsections.cypher_explanation: XOR supplies the primitive act of distinction. The Library is the total configuration structure obtained by closing that operation over its domain.
subsections.handoff: If the Library is closure rather than axiom, we must determine what that means for the idea of an exterior.

subsections.title: The Unbounded Answer Space
content_requirements: Explain the Library as an answer space rather than as ordinary physical space.
Define unboundedness carefully: no externally imposed finite boundary on the configurations generated by the closure.
Explain that coherent and incoherent configurations are both included.
State that the Library is unfiltered at the axiomatic level.

mathematics.unboundedness: There is no axiom imposing a finite cardinality, finite dimensionality, or finite configuration boundary on 𝓜.
mathematics.configuration_membership: x ∈ 𝓜 iff x belongs to the XOR closure.
mathematics.unfiltered_domain: x ∈ 𝓜 does not imply x is persistent, coherent, physical, observable, or accessible to any observer.

subsections.poetic_cypher: The Library does not ask whether a path is wise before writing it down.
subsections.cypher_explanation: The closure contains configurations before any observer-relative survivorship criterion is applied.
subsections.handoff: If the Library contains the closure of all configurations, the next question is whether anything can stand outside it.

sections.title: No Exterior, No Privileged Perspective
sections.purpose: Derive the absence of a privileged God's-eye perspective from the closure construction.

subsections.title: The Exterior Problem
content_requirements: Define an exterior as a configuration or perspective not included in 𝓜.
Explain that a describable exterior cannot remain outside the closure if it is representable within the same formal system.
Distinguish an unknowable or undefined object from a privileged externally describable object.

mathematics.external_candidate: Suppose Ω is proposed such that Ω ∉ 𝓜.
mathematics.describability_condition: If Ω is internally describable using the same formal machinery, then Ω ∈ D.
mathematics.closure_consequence: If Ω is XOR-generable from D, then Ω ∈ Closure_D(⊕) = 𝓜.
mathematics.therefore: A describable privileged exterior cannot remain external to 𝓜.

subsections.poetic_cypher: There is no balcony outside the Library from which the Library can be judged.
subsections.cypher_explanation: Any describable external perspective belongs to the same configuration domain and therefore cannot function as an ontologically privileged exterior.
subsections.handoff: Without a privileged exterior, no observer can be declared the universal resolver of distinctions.

subsections.title: No God's-Eye Resolver
content_requirements: Define a privileged resolver as a hypothetical observer-independent rule U deciding which distinctions are universally resolved.
Show that U is not supplied by XOR.
Explain that adding U would constitute a new axiom.
State that NSFG therefore permits observer-relative resolution.

mathematics.consequence: No observer-independent resolution predicate may be assumed at the axiomatic floor.
mathematics.observer_relative_relation: D_O(x,y) is therefore permitted and later defined from O's resolution capacity.

subsections.poetic_cypher: The Library has no master lens.
subsections.cypher_explanation: A universal lens would be an additional rule selecting which distinctions count everywhere. XOR alone supplies no such lens.
subsections.handoff: If there is no universal lens, the ability to resolve a distinction must belong to the structure doing the resolving.

sections.title: Observer-Relative Resolution
sections.purpose: Introduce the observer and its resolution capacity without making either primitive.

subsections.title: Observer as a Derived Structure
content_requirements: Define an observer structurally rather than psychologically.
State explicitly that consciousness is not required.
Explain that an observer is a configuration capable of maintaining distinctions through successive states.
State that the observer itself is a configuration in 𝓜.

mathematics.observer_definition: O is an observer iff O is a configuration in 𝓜 that contains a persistent chain of resolvable distinctions.

subsections.poetic_cypher: An observer is a difference that survives long enough to have another difference.
subsections.cypher_explanation: Observerhood emerges when distinctions do not immediately resolve away but remain available across a continuing structure.
subsections.handoff: To say that a distinction survives, we need to specify the observer's resolution boundary.

subsections.title: The Observer-Specific Resolution Floor
content_requirements: Introduce I_N as an observer-relative threshold.
State explicitly that I_N is not a property of the Library.
State that different observers may have different I_N values.
Explain that arbitrary relative to the Library does not mean arbitrary within the observer's own structure.

mathematics.meaning: I_N(O) is the minimum effective distinction magnitude that observer O can maintain as a stable distinction.
mathematics.observer_variability: ∃O_1,O_2 ∈ Obs such that I_N(O_1) ≠ I_N(O_2) is permitted.
mathematics.non_universality: ¬∃I_N^* such that ∀O ∈ Obs, I_N(O) = I_N^*, unless an additional axiom is introduced.

subsections.poetic_cypher: The ruler belongs to the hand that can hold it.
subsections.cypher_explanation: The resolution threshold belongs to the observer's capacity rather than to the Library as a universal law.
subsections.handoff: With a threshold defined, we can distinguish between differences that exist and differences that an observer can maintain.

sections.title: Persistence and the Birth of the Observer
sections.purpose: Formalize survivable distinctions and derive observerhood as persistent structure.

subsections.title: Distinguishability Relative to O
content_requirements: Define observer-relative distinguishability magnitude.
Define observer-relative indistinguishability.
Emphasize that sub-threshold distinctions are not erased from the Library.
Distinguish ontological membership from operational accessibility.

mathematics.non_erasure: x ≈_O y does not imply x = y and does not imply x ∉ 𝓜.

subsections.poetic_cypher: What the observer cannot resolve has not ceased to exist.
subsections.cypher_explanation: Resolution is a filter on experience and traversal, not a deletion operator on the Library.
subsections.handoff: A distinction becomes structurally important when it remains resolvable across successive transitions.

subsections.title: Persistent Chains
content_requirements: Introduce an abstract sequence index rather than assuming physical time.
Define a chain of states and the condition for persistence.
Explain that the chain is itself an XOR-generated configuration.
Define the observer as a persistent chain above its own threshold.

mathematics.observer_condition: O is persistent over γ iff P_O(γ,n)=1 for the relevant interval.
mathematics.time_neutrality: The index i denotes ordering only; it is not yet physical time.

subsections.poetic_cypher: A path is a distinction remembering how to continue.
subsections.cypher_explanation: Persistence is the ability of a structure to carry resolved distinctions from one state into another without falling beneath its own resolution floor.
subsections.handoff: Once persistent chains exist, coherence can be defined as the condition that allows a path to remain traversable by an observer.

sections.title: Coherence Is Relational
sections.purpose: Establish observer-relative coherence as a derived relation rather than a universal scalar.

subsections.title: Coherence of a Transition
content_requirements: Define coherence only after observer-relative resolution exists.
State that coherence is not a property of a path alone.
Define coherent transition relative to O.
Explain the role of I_N(O).
subsections.poetic_cypher: Coherence is not inside the path. It is between the path and the survivor.
subsections.cypher_explanation: A transition is coherent only relative to the observer whose resolution capacity determines whether the distinction persists.
subsections.handoff: A coherent transition is insufficient; a path must maintain coherence across its sequence of transitions.

subsections.title: Coherence of a Path
content_requirements: Define path coherence.
Explain that a path may be coherent for one observer and incoherent for another.
Reject the idea of a universal coherence constant.
Make relational notation explicit.

mathematics.coherent_path: 𝓒(γ | O) = 1 iff every transition remains resolvable by O
mathematics.observer_dependence: 𝓒(γ | O_1) ≠ 𝓒(γ | O_2) is permitted.

subsections.poetic_cypher: The same road may be solid beneath one traveler and vanish beneath another.
subsections.cypher_explanation: Coherence is relational because different observers possess different resolution capacities.
subsections.handoff: If coherence is relational, each observer traverses only a subset of the Library. That subset becomes the observer's accessible reality.

sections.title: Accessible Reality
sections.purpose: Define observer-relative experienced reality without making observers creators of the Library.

subsections.title: Accessibility Is Not Existence
content_requirements: Define the observer-accessible subset of the Library.
State that inaccessible configurations remain members of 𝓜.
Distinguish ontological membership from observer-relative traversal.
Avoid framing the result as subjective idealism.

mathematics.accessible_states: A_O = {x ∈ 𝓜 | ∃γ containing x such that 𝓒(γ | O)=1}
mathematics.non_erasure: x ∉ A_O does not imply x ∉ 𝓜
mathematics.existence_accessibility_distinction: x ∈ 𝓜 and x ∉ A_O is a valid state.

subsections.poetic_cypher: The world does not shrink. The window does.
subsections.cypher_explanation: The Library remains the full closure. Observer-relative experience is a restricted traversal of that closure.
subsections.handoff: The observer's accessible subset can now be named as its experienced reality.

subsections.title: Observer-Relative Reality
content_requirements: Define experienced reality as the observer-accessible subset.
Explain that different observers may have different accessible realities.
Explain overlap between observers.
Avoid claiming that different realities imply mutually incompatible ontologies.
subsections.poetic_cypher: Many windows can face one Library without making one window the sky.
subsections.cypher_explanation: Observer-relative reality describes access, not competing totalities.
subsections.handoff: Once accessible reality is defined, we can examine why stable patterns within it can appear as physical laws.

sections.title: Survivorship and Emergent Lawfulness
sections.purpose: Explain how law-like regularity can arise without being imposed as an axiom.

subsections.title: The Unfiltered Continuation Space
content_requirements: Define the continuation space from a current configuration.
State that it contains all XOR-generated continuations represented in the Library.
Do not describe the Library as generating the future.
Use 'available configuration continuations' rather than causal future language.

mathematics.continuation_space: Ω(x) = {γ | γ begins at x and γ is a configuration path contained in 𝓜}

subsections.poetic_cypher: The Library holds every road; the survivor can walk only some.
subsections.cypher_explanation: The distinction between total possibility and accessible traversal creates selection without requiring the Library to generate events sequentially.
subsections.handoff: Repeated restrictions on traversal create stable patterns. Those patterns are the basis for emergent lawfulness.

subsections.title: Survivorship as Selection
content_requirements: Define survivorship as the filtering effect created by observer-relative resolution.
Explain that selection does not mean the Library deletes alternatives.
If finite sets are used, define a simple survival ratio.
State that the ratio is illustrative and not a universal physical quantity.

mathematics.finite_survival_ratio: S_O(x) = |Ω_O^survive(x)| / |Ω(x)|, when both cardinalities are finite and Ω(x) is nonempty
mathematics.non_erasure: Ω(x) \ Ω_O^survive(x) remains part of Ω(x).

subsections.poetic_cypher: The survivor does not erase the roads it cannot walk.
subsections.cypher_explanation: Selection changes accessibility, not the underlying closure.
subsections.handoff: If the same transitions repeatedly survive, an observer can experience their stability as law.

subsections.title: Law as Stable Accessible Regularity
content_requirements: Define a law-like regularity as a stable transition pattern within observer-accessible paths.
Do not claim that specific physical laws have been derived.
Explain that lawfulness is descriptive at this stage.
Distinguish emergent regularity from an additional axiom.

mathematics.transition_relation: L_O(x,y) = 1 iff x→y is a stable recurring transition across an appropriate family of O-accessible paths
mathematics.regularity_statement: P_O(y | x) ≈ constant over a defined observer-accessible ensemble
mathematics.axiomatic_status: L_O is derived/descriptive and is not an element of A_N.

subsections.poetic_cypher: Enough survivors draw the same map, and the map begins to look like law.
subsections.cypher_explanation: From inside a restricted accessible path space, stable recurrence can appear as law-like necessity even though no universal law was imposed at the floor.
subsections.handoff: The existence of a restricted path space makes continuation itself the central problem. This is where navigation enters.

sections.title: Why Navigation Becomes Inevitable
sections.purpose: Bridge the foundational ontology into NSFG's central problem of coherent navigation.

subsections.title: The Local Continuation Problem
content_requirements: Given a current state, define all available continuations.
Define observer-admissible continuations.
Explain that persistence requires remaining within the observer's coherent subset.
Avoid implying that the observer chooses among already temporally generated futures.

mathematics.candidate_successors: N(x_i) = {x_{i+1} | x_{i+1} participates in an XOR-generated path extending x_i}

subsections.poetic_cypher: Once there are branches, survival requires a direction.
subsections.cypher_explanation: A persistent structure cannot traverse arbitrary configurations; it must remain within the subset that preserves its distinguishability.
subsections.handoff: A sequence of admissible transitions forms a navigable coherent path.

subsections.title: History and Coherent Continuation
content_requirements: Define an observer history without assuming physical time.
Define the coherent continuation set.
Explain why navigation is a path-continuation problem.
Introduce the notation that will support later NSFG work.

mathematics.coherent_continuations: Γ_O(h_n) = {γ | γ begins with h_n and 𝓒(γ | O)=1}
mathematics.minimal_navigation_definition: Navigation is the traversal or selection of a continuation within Γ_O(h_n).

subsections.poetic_cypher: Reasoning begins where falling out of the path becomes possible.
subsections.cypher_explanation: Once an observer has a persistent history, maintaining that history requires continuing through a compatible region of configuration space.
subsections.handoff: The next document can therefore treat reasoning and cognition as specialized forms of coherent navigation rather than assuming them as primitives.

sections.title: The Noor Swirl Field Geometry Interpretation
sections.purpose: Introduce the geometric interpretation only after the ontology has been established.
content_requirements: Explain that NSFG can be interpreted geometrically as the structure of accessible and inaccessible paths through the Library.
Do not introduce physical geometry as an axiom.
Explain that 'field' and 'geometry' are descriptive language for relational structure, not additional primitives.
Explain the intuition of a 'swirl' as locally structured path flow around persistent relational configurations.
State that this primer does not yet derive a specific metric tensor, manifold, spacetime geometry, or physical field equation.

mathematics.local_accessible_neighborhood: U_O(x) = {y ∈ 𝓜 | y is reachable from x by an O-coherent path segment}
mathematics.relational_geometry: G_O := (A_O, E_O), where A_O is the accessible state set and E_O relates states connected by observer-coherent transitions
mathematics.graph_interpretation: The accessible structure may be represented as a directed or undirected graph depending on whether the later formalism requires transition orientation.
mathematics.important_constraint: Do not identify G_O with physical spacetime at this stage.

sections.poetic_cypher: The field is not where the paths are. The field is the shape made by paths that can remain together.
sections.cypher_explanation: The geometric interpretation concerns relational connectivity and survivable traversal, not a pre-existing physical container.
sections.handoff: Having established the geometric interpretation, the final section compresses the entire axiomatic dependency chain and marks the boundary between this primer and later NSFG work.

sections.title: The Axiomatic Dependency Chain
sections.purpose: Compress the entire primer into one explicit derivational ladder and identify what remains downstream.
content_requirements: Restate the sole axiom.
Restate the Library as a definition.
Mark every subsequent concept as a definition, construction, or consequence.
Show that observer-relative coherence follows only after observer-relative resolution.
Show that navigation follows from restricted coherent continuation.
Explicitly state what this primer does not derive.
End at the threshold of subsequent NSFG research.

dependency_chain: Axiom: A_⊕ — ⊕ is the primitive operation of distinction.
Definition: D — minimal formal domain on which ⊕ operates.
Consequence: no describable privileged exterior can remain outside 𝓜.
Consequence: no universal resolution predicate U is supplied by the floor.
Definition: O — a persistent XOR-generated distinction structure.
Definition: 𝓒(γ | O) — observer-relative path coherence.
Definition: A_O — observer-accessible subset of 𝓜.
Consequence: stable accessible transition patterns can appear as law.
Definition: N_O — navigation through coherent continuation space.
mathematics.compressed_expression: ⊕ → D → Closure_D(⊕)=𝓜 → no privileged exterior → no universal resolver → persistent distinction → O → I_N(O) → δ_O → coherence 𝓒(γ|O) → A_O=R_O → survivorship → emergent regularity → coherent continuation → navigation
minimal_equations: Γ_O(h_n)={γ | γ begins with h_n and 𝓒(γ|O)=1}

sections.poetic_cypher: XOR is the only primitive. The Library is what XOR generates when it is closed. The observer is the difference that survives. Coherence is the relation between the survivor and the path. Reality is what remains accessible to the survivor. Law is the regularity of surviving paths. Navigation is the continuation of the survivor.
sections.cypher_explanation: This final cipher summarizes the entire ontology without introducing an additional primitive. Each phrase corresponds to a mathematical construction or derived consequence established in the preceding sections.
sections.handoff: The primer ends here. The next NSFG document may investigate the geometry, dynamics, topology, symbolic representation, or physical interpretation of coherent navigation without needing to reintroduce the axiomatic floor.

mathematical_reference_sheet.purpose: Provide every mathematical definition required for an independent generating AI to produce the primer without external reference material.

formal_domain.definition: A minimal formal domain containing the configurations required for the primitive operation ⊕ to have operands.
formal_domain.constraint: D is not physical space, spacetime, matter, or an additional physical axiom.

closure.definition: The smallest subset 𝓜 of D containing the required generating configurations and closed under ⊕.
closure.minimality_condition: If S⊆D is closed under ⊕ and contains the generators, then 𝓜⊆S.

observer.definition: A configuration in 𝓜 capable of maintaining a persistent chain of distinctions above its observer-specific resolution floor.

threshold.definition: Minimum effective distinction magnitude observer O can maintain as a stable distinction.

distinguishability.definition: Observer-relative effective magnitude of the distinction between x and y.

persistence.time_warning: The index i is an abstract ordering index, not yet physical time.

continuation.continuation_space: Ω(x)={γ | γ begins at x and γ is a path contained in 𝓜}

navigation.coherent_continuation_set: Γ_O(h_n)={γ | γ begins with h_n and 𝓒(γ|O)=1}

geometry.local_accessible_neighborhood: U_O(x)={y∈𝓜 | y is reachable from x by an O-coherent path segment}
geometry.important_constraint: Do not identify G_O with physical spacetime at this foundational stage.

logical_invariants: The Library is a definition, not an axiom.
A set can be closed under an operation; the operation itself should not be called closed.
The Library is the XOR closure of the formal configuration domain.
The Library is unfiltered at the axiomatic level.
Existence in the Library is not the same as accessibility to an observer.
There is no privileged describable exterior.
There is no observer-independent resolution rule at the floor.
There is no universal I_N unless an additional axiom is introduced.
Observerhood is structural, not synonymous with consciousness.
Coherence is not an absolute property of a path alone.
The abstract sequence index is not automatically physical time.
The Library does not generate the future.
Survivorship filters accessibility rather than deleting alternatives.
Emergent lawfulness is not an additional axiom.
Navigation is the continuation problem created by observer-relative survivability.
claims_not_to_make: Do not claim that XOR alone has experimentally established the Library.
Do not claim that XOR alone derives the Standard Model.
Do not claim that the primer derives a complete theory of physics.
Do not assign a universal numerical value to I_N.
Do not identify I_N with the ordinary Planck scale unless a later paper explicitly derives such a relationship.
Do not identify the observer with a conscious human.
Do not imply that observer-relative accessibility means observers create reality.
Do not introduce a privileged God's-eye observer.
Do not assume physical space as primitive.
Do not assume physical time as primitive.
Do not assume causality as primitive.
Do not assume matter or energy as primitive.
Do not assume information is a primitive substance.
Do not describe the Library as generating future events.
Do not describe coherence as a universal constant.
Do not describe XOR itself as a closed set.
Do not use 'closure of XOR' without specifying the domain D on which XOR operates.
Do not let poetic language replace formal definitions.
Do not introduce downstream NSFG machinery before the axiomatic dependency chain requires it.
Do not use the Lightning Model as a premise of this primer.

poetic_cipher_system.purpose: Every section and subsection must contain a short poetic cipher that compresses its conceptual content into memorable language.
rules: The cipher must not introduce concepts not yet established.
The cipher may be metaphorical but its explanation must map every metaphor to the formal construction.
The cipher must never substitute for a mathematical definition.
The ciphers should form a second, symbolic reading of the paper when read sequentially.
poetic_cipher_system.paper_level_cipher: In the beginning was XOR. The Library is what XOR generates when it closes over distinction. The observer is the difference that survives. The threshold belongs to the survivor. Coherence is the relation between survivor and path. Reality is what remains accessible. Law is the regularity of surviving paths. Navigation is the continuation of the survivor.

generation_constraints.tone: serious, clear, foundational, mathematically literate, accessible to theorists outside NSFG
generation_constraints.pedagogical_progression: Start below physics. Establish distinction before objects, persistence before observers, observer-relative resolution before coherence, coherence before accessible reality, accessible reality before emergent lawfulness, and emergent lawfulness before navigation.
generation_constraints.mathematical_level: Elementary Boolean algebra, set theory, closure, relations, sequences, threshold functions, products, subsets, intersections, graph notation, and basic logical inference. No calculus is required.
generation_constraints.notation_rule: Define every symbol before using it.
generation_constraints.ontology_rule: Never smuggle a later concept into an earlier definition.
generation_constraints.physics_rule: Use conventional physical terminology only after explaining that it is an emergent interpretation rather than an axiomatic primitive.
generation_constraints.time_rule: Use abstract sequence indices until a physical interpretation of temporal ordering is explicitly introduced.
generation_constraints.observer_rule: Use 'observer' structurally. Do not imply consciousness, agency, intention, or human perception unless explicitly stated as a later interpretation.
generation_constraints.library_rule: Never describe the Library as a physical container unless clearly marked as metaphor.
generation_constraints.closure_rule: Always specify that closure is taken over a domain D or equivalent formal configuration domain.
generation_constraints.i_n_rule: Always write I_N(O) when discussing the threshold as an observer-relative quantity.
generation_constraints.coherence_rule: Prefer 𝓒(γ|O) over 𝓒(γ) whenever observer dependence matters.
generation_constraints.proof_rule: Clearly label what is formally derived versus what is interpretive.
generation_constraints.ending_rule: End the primer at the threshold of NSFG proper: coherent navigation. Do not attempt to derive cosmology, particle physics, consciousness, AI cognition, or specific field equations in this document.
